definition: Eyes of Things (EoT) is the name of a project funded by the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Programme under grant agreement number 643924.
details: The purpose of the project, which is funded under the Smart Cyber-physical systems topic, is to develop a generic hardware-software platform for embedded, efficient (i.e. battery-operated, wearable, mobile), computer vision, including deep learning inference. On November 29, 2018, the European Space Agency announced that it was testing the suitability of the device for space applications in advance of a flight in a Cubesat.

explainer.lead: Eyes of Things (EoT) is an EU-funded project to build a reusable hardware and software platform for computer vision on small, power-limited devices. It matters because tasks such as deep-learning inference must run efficiently when a device is wearable, mobile, or battery-operated.

tiers.eli5: EoT is like a compact electronic brain that helps small gadgets understand what they see. Instead of needing a large computer, it is designed for devices that run on batteries or can be worn. It was also tested to see whether it could work on a tiny satellite.
tiers.practitioner: EoT targets embedded computer vision through a generic hardware-software platform, including efficient deep-learning inference. The design setting is battery-operated, wearable, or mobile equipment, where power use and embedded operation are central constraints. Its announced ESA testing concerned suitability for space use, not a completed CubeSat deployment.
tiers.paperLevel: EoT is defined as a generic hardware-software platform for efficient embedded computer vision, with deep-learning inference included among its target capabilities. The project was funded under Horizon 2020 grant agreement 643924 in the Smart Cyber-physical Systems topic. Its space-application readiness remained under evaluation when ESA announced its testing on November 29, 2018.

explainer.example: On November 29, 2018, ESA announced that it was testing the EoT device's suitability for space applications before a flight in a CubeSat, a concrete test of whether efficient embedded vision could be used beyond everyday mobile devices.

usedIn.name: Embedded computer vision
usedIn.detail: The platform is intended to bring vision processing directly onto efficient embedded devices.

usedIn.name: Wearable and mobile systems
usedIn.detail: Battery operation and mobility are explicit targets of the project.

usedIn.name: Space systems
usedIn.detail: ESA tested the device's suitability for space applications ahead of a planned CubeSat flight.

explainer.intuition: Put the vision processing inside the small device itself, using hardware and software designed to work efficiently within its limited power budget.
howItWorks: An embedded device receives visual input.
The EoT hardware-software platform processes that input.
Deep-learning inference can run as part of the vision workload.
The design prioritizes efficiency for battery-powered, wearable, and mobile operation.
explainer.whyItMatters: A generic platform can support vision and deep-learning inference on devices where size, mobility, and battery power constrain what can run locally.
misconceptions: EoT is a project to develop a platform, not just a single deep-learning model.
Deep-learning inference is one capability, not the project's entire scope.
ESA's announcement described testing and a planned CubeSat flight, not a proven operational deployment.

diagram.caption: EoT combines hardware and software to run embedded vision, including deep-learning inference, on efficient small devices.
